key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: In line with this commitment, we today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: Compared with March, staff have revised up their baseline projection for inflation in 2026 and 2027 owing to a higher path for energy prices, which, to some extent, is expected to feed into food, goods and services inflation.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: Domestic cost pressures eased in the first quarter, supported by slower growth in wages and profits.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: And even in the milder scenario, the 25-basis-point cut is completely warranted and justified.

briefing:
The ECB raised its key interest rates by 25 basis points. The Hawk & Dove stance index rates the press conference as slightly hawkish: it ranks at the 77th percentile of the 53 press conferences held since December 2019, up from the 69th percentile at the previous meeting on 30 April 2026. The monetary policy statement ranks at the 66th percentile and the answers in the Q&A at the 92nd.

The ECB expects headline inflation to average 3.0 per cent in 2026, 2.3 per cent in 2027 and 2.0 per cent in 2028 [1]. The outlook remains uncertain, with upside risks for inflation and downside risks for economic growth [2]. The ECB highlighted that the risks to the growth outlook are to the downside, mainly owing to the war in the Middle East, which has added to the volatile global policy environment [3].

The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside, and if energy prices were to rise by more and for longer than currently expected, euro area inflation would increase further [4]. The ECB will closely monitor the situation and follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach to determining the appropriate monetary policy stance [5].
